subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria

Hi Sarah — great conversation earlier. Thanks for the time. Below is a short recap plus the proposed POC observability scope and next steps so we can align before kickoff.

POC goal (proposed): Prove Redwood inference can serve FintechX transaction enrichment calls at production-like scale while meeting latency SLOs and providing end-to-end observability for production readiness.

Proposed success criteria (suggested):
- 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for enrichment path under target QPS (to be confirmed)
- No functional regressions vs your golden prompt set (sample test harness)
- End-to-end tracing available for 100% of sampled requests with span breakdowns for network/model/runtime
- Dashboards with token-level cost, per-model latency by route, error rate < 0.5%
- Log export to your Splunk/GCP project for audit and retention (30d by default)

Observability scope (what Redwood will provide):
- Pre-built Grafana dashboard templates (latency, throughput, error rate, cost)
- Distributed tracing spans with trace ids propagated through enrichment flow
- Structured JSON logs with request_id, model_id, input_hash, latency_ms, tokens_in/out, error fields
- Export adapter to your Splunk/GCP bucket (config + sample pipeline)
- Alerting runbook and recommended thresholds for the POC

Proposed timeline: 2-week POC start window (we're flexible):
- Week 0: kickoff + access (credentials, sample traffic, contact list)
- Week 1: instrumentation + baseline run (low load)
- Week 2: production-scale soak + evaluation, final review

Owners / asks from FintechX:
- Provide a sample traffic generator and golden prompt set (JSON)
- Point us to Splunk or GCP logging project for export (or we can ship logs to our S3 staging)
- Designate an eng owner for trace header propagation (e.g., X-Trace-Id)

Attachments: poc_observability_checklist.xlsx (checklist), redwood_onboarding_instrumentation_guide.pdf (how-to)

Could you confirm the success criteria above, the proposed timeline, and the primary eng contact (who will own trace + log access)? If you're good we can schedule a 30-minute kickoff Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Li <peter.li@fintechx.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. This aligns closely with what we discussed. A few notes from our side:

Confirmed success criteria (we propose slight tweaks):
- P99 latency target: <= 300ms for enrichment path at our nominal QPS (we'll share target QPS in follow-up)
- Functional regression: we will provide a 250-case golden prompt set and automated comparison script
- Tracing: want 100% of sampled requests instrumented, but please include sampling config (we prefer 10% initial sampling with on-demand full traces for failures)
- Error budget: <= 0.5% errors, with an SLO alert if exceeded for 15min

Timeline: 2 weeks is fine but can extend to 3 if we need more soak time. We prefer a 3-week window (instrumentation + low-load baseline + ramp to peak + customer validation).

Owners:
- FintechX eng owner: Peter Li (peter.li@fintechx.com) — will own trace header propagation and sample traffic
- Security contact for log access and retention: our infra security lead, Naomi Wu (naomi.wu@fintechx.com) — she'll approve Splunk access and retention policy

Questions / asks for Redwood:
- Can you share the Grafana dashboard JSONs ahead of kickoff so our SRE can pre-provision dashboards?
- We need a short runbook for how to map your request_ids to our internal transaction ids.

If you can send an updated plan reflecting 3-week timeline + sampling config I'll route it to our SRE and security. Kickoff Wednesday 29 Jul at 10am PT works for us (tentative).

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Kim | Head of Product, FintechX

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Success Criteria (updated plan + deliverables)

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the feedback. Per your ask we've adjusted to a 3-week POC and added a sampling config. Below is the updated observability plan and the deliverables Redwood will provide prior to kickoff on Wed 2026-07-29 10:00 PT (tentative).

Updated timeline (3-week):
- Week 0 (kickoff, day 0-2): access exchange, SSO/credentials, pre-provision Grafana dashboards, import alerting rules
- Week 1 (instrumentation & low-load baseline): deploy Redwood sidecar, validate trace header propagation, enable 10% sampling
- Week 2 (ramp): ramp to target QPS each day, monitor P99 and error rate, increase sampling to 25% for peak windows
- Week 3 (soak & validation): 48-72h soak at target load, run golden prompt regression tests, final review

Deliverables (Redwood):
- Grafana dashboard JSONs (latency, tokens, cost, errors) — will share link today
- Tracing spec + OpenTelemetry span names and attributes (we'll include sample instrumentation snippets)
- Structured log schema + Log export connector (Splunk/GCP)
- Alerting thresholds and runbook (SLO breach playbook)
- Post-POC report template (latency percentiles, token costs, failure analysis)

Observability specifics (dashboard/metric list):
- Dashboards:
  - Inference Overview: total requests, avg latency, P50/P90/P99 latency, throughput (req/s), tokens in/out, cost per 1k tokens
  - Per-route performance: latency and error rate by route/model_id
  - System health: GPU utilization, queue depth, batching efficiency, memory pressure
  - Logging & Errors: error types, top stack traces, request_id mapping

- Tracing:
  - Span breakdown: client -> network -> runtime -> model_inference -> postproc
  - Attributes: request_id, finx_transaction_id (your id), model_id, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms
  - Sampling: default 10% (configurable), full sampling for requests that trigger errors or exceed latency thresholds

- Logs: structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, request_id, trace_id, finx_transaction_id, latency_ms, model_id, error_code, payload_hash. Export connector to Splunk with newline-delimited JSON. Retention default 30d; can be configured by Naomi/security.

Alerting suggestions:
- P99 latency > 300ms for > 15m -> paged to SRE
- Error rate > 0.5% over 10m -> page and rollback guidance
- Batch drop events -> page infra on-call

Action items / next steps:
1) Marissa: share Grafana JSONs + instrumentation guide (attached) — ACTION: by EOD today
2) Peter (FintechX): share target QPS, sample traffic generator, and golden prompt set — ACTION: before kickoff
3) Naomi (FintechX security): confirm Splunk/GCP export policy and retention — ACTION: before kickoff
4) Marcus/Aditya (Redwood): coordinate sampling and rate-limit guardrails during ramp — ACTION: pre-kickoff prep

Attachments referenced: poc_observability_checklist.xlsx, redwood_onboarding_instrumentation_guide.pdf (both attached to this thread). Grafana JSONs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-poc-observability
